doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Closing remarks
summary: Woods and Powell close, discussing respect for African American musicians and thanking each other.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I would like to just say as we close here, that these interviews with some of the greatest living jazz musicians there are, have come about particularly to rectify some of the injustices that have been done to African American musicians. And I would like to see that taken care of. And I would like to see people get their due. And when I was asked to © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

participate on these particular interviews, someone asked me about that. And I broke down in tears and I said these people need their respect. And so I believe and I trust that even as we are looking into this camera right now, you are getting some that you richly deserve.

Oh, well, I’ll tell you, the fact that you allowed me to be able to voice it, means that it’s possible to change. If I didn’t get a chance to voice it, nobody would get a chance to see it. Certainly that’s just my idea and maybe I could walk around a bitter old man that nobody wanted. But once you put an idea out there, and especially in an institution of learning, there’s no telling where that idea can go because that’s why I guess when we all do these interviews, we try to do them as purely as possible, and give as honest answers—well we all know how to be politicians, but we hope that we can really impart some of our true feelings. And you have given me the opportunity to do that so I thank you for it.
And thank you. And that concludes our interview with Benny Powell. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
